pal/spotify.caption: The pal registry · Media
pal/spotify.title: Spotify
pal/spotify.markdown:
Search, play, queue, like and add to playlists on Spotify from the keyboard, with lyrics that follow the song and a bar item that shows the line playing.

## What it does

- Search tracks, artists, albums, playlists and podcasts as you type; `enter` plays, `cmd+enter` queues
- Like with `cmd+l`, add to a playlist with `cmd+p`, open in Spotify with `cmd+o`
- Your playlists, liked songs, recently played, top tracks, devices and the queue
- Synced lyrics around the line playing, with the cover, progress and playback on keys
- Play, pause, skip and like from the root, plus a row for each pinned playlist
- A bar item with the track or the lyric line playing

## Palettes

- Lyrics
- Search Spotify
- Playlists
- Library
- Spotify Devices
- Queue
- Spotify

![The lyrics view: the cover, the progress, the line playing bright among the lines around it](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/spotify/screenshots/1-lyrics.png)
![Search: tracks, artists, albums, playlists and podcasts as sections](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/spotify/screenshots/2-search.png)
![Playlists: yours and the followed ones; cmd+enter lists a playlist's tracks](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/spotify/screenshots/3-playlists.png)
![Library: Liked Songs newest first, the other filters on Tab](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/spotify/screenshots/4-library.png)
![The queue: what plays now, what comes next, Enter skips to a row](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/spotify/screenshots/5-queue.png)

featured:pal/solitaire.caption: The pal registry · Fun
featured:pal/solitaire.title: Solitaire
featured:pal/solitaire.markdown:
Klondike on a felt table: drag the cards with the mouse, or play with the arrows and Enter. Draw one or three, unlimited passes and undo; the game and your record are kept.

## What it does

- Drag cards and runs with the mouse; the piles they can go on light up
- Keyboard play with the arrows and `enter`; `enter` twice sends a card where it belongs
- Cards glide and flip, and a win bounces them off the foundations
- Draw one or three, unlimited passes, and undo with `U` or `backspace`
- Finishes by itself once every card is face up
- Your moves, time and games won are kept, and the game waits where you left it

## Palettes

- Solitaire

![A fresh deal: the cursor on the stock, the moves, the time and the record beside the table](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/solitaire/screenshots/1-deal.png)
![54 moves in: the cursor takes 4 cards of a run, the title line names them](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/solitaire/screenshots/2-game.png)
![Enter picks the run up: it lifts, and the pile it can go on lights up](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/solitaire/screenshots/3-carry.png)
![Won: every card home, the moves and the time, Enter deals again](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/solitaire/screenshots/4-won.png)

featured:pal/calendar.caption: The pal registry · Productivity
featured:pal/calendar.title: Calendar
featured:pal/calendar.markdown:
Your upcoming events with the current one marked, and a meeting about to start at the top of the panel, one key to join the call. Add events with a form or one typed line like `standup tomorrow 10:00`.

## What it does

- Today and My Schedule: events in order, each tagged `in 12 min`, `now` or `over`
- `enter` joins the Zoom, Meet, Teams or Webex call, or opens the event
- A call about to start sits at the top of the panel before you type anything
- The next event on the menu bar, amber inside 15 minutes and red inside 5; a click joins
- Add events by form or one line (`dentist fri 2pm-3pm`); delete one after a confirmation
- Reads Calendar.app's accounts on macOS, `khal` on Linux, or Google Calendar directly

## Palettes

- My Schedule
- Today
- Quick Add Event

![What is left of today and the days after, the next event tagged with how soon, calls tagged Join](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/calendar/screenshots/1-schedule.png)

![New event: a title, a day in words, the times from the next quarter hour, the calendar](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/calendar/screenshots/3-new.png)
![Today: the whole day in order, what is over greyed, the rest with how long until it starts](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/calendar/screenshots/4-today.png)

featured:pal/translate.caption: The pal registry · Productivity
featured:pal/translate.title: Translate
featured:pal/translate.markdown:
Translate what you type, the selected text or the clipboard, with the language detected as you type. Alternatives, dictionary entries and romanisation included; uses Google Translate without a key, or DeepL with one.

## What it does

- Translates as you type, the source detected, into the language you set or the system's
- Name the target inline: `tr: hello`, `>de hello`, `en>tr merhaba`; works at the root too
- With nothing typed, starts from the selected text or the newest clipboard text
- `enter` copies, `cmd+enter` pastes, `cmd+shift+s` reads it aloud; Swap translates the result back
- Alternatives, dictionary entries for a single word, and romanisation for non-Latin scripts
- Google Translate needs no key (unofficial, some networks are refused), or DeepL with a free key; a history of what you used

## Palettes

- Translate
- Translation History

![>ja hello: the Japanese with its romanisation and the dictionary entry](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/translate/screenshots/3-romanisation.png)

![Translation History: what was copied or spoken, newest first](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/translate/screenshots/5-history.png)

pal/apps.caption: Comes with pal · Productivity
pal/apps.title: Applications
pal/apps.markdown:
Launch any installed app by name, with its own icon. On macOS, running apps can be quit or hidden and the System Settings panes are rows too; on Linux, an app's own actions are one key away.

## What it does

- Every app in your Applications folders on macOS, every `.desktop` entry and flatpak on Linux
- Found by name or bundle id, so `Chrome` or `com.apple.` both work
- Running apps are tagged, with Quit (`cmd+q`) and Hide (`cmd+h`)
- System Settings panes as rows on macOS, found by words like `dark mode` or `dns`
- On Linux, an app's own actions (`New Private Window`) as secondary actions
- `cmd+i` shows where it lives, its version, bundle id and processes

## Palettes

- Applications

![The applications by name, the running ones tagged](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/apps/screenshots/1-list.png)
![Typing at the root finds an app by its bundle id as well as its name: ical is Calendar (com.apple.iCal)](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/apps/screenshots/2-search.png)
![A running app: Open, Quit, Hide, Reveal in Finder, Copy path, Copy bundle id](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/apps/screenshots/3-actions.png)
![The System Settings panes are rows too, found by what they hold: network finds Network and Wi-Fi](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/apps/screenshots/4-panes.png)
![An app's details (cmd+i): its folder, running and its version, the bundle id and processes](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/apps/screenshots/5-detail.png)

pal/bookmarks.caption: Comes with pal · Productivity
pal/bookmarks.title: Bookmarks
pal/bookmarks.markdown:
Search the bookmarks of every browser you use, plus links of your own, and open one in the browser it came from. A second list searches your browsing history.

## What it does

- Chrome, Brave, Edge, Chromium, Vivaldi, Arc, Safari and Firefox, every profile
- Your own links from a JSON file, with names, keywords and icons
- Found by name, address or folder; a link saved twice is listed once
- Open it, open it in the browser it came from, or copy it plain or as a markdown link
- Browser History: search pages you visited in Chrome-family browsers and Firefox, newest first

## Palettes

pal/browser-tabs.caption: Comes with pal · Productivity
pal/browser-tabs.title: Browser Tabs
pal/browser-tabs.markdown:
Every tab open in your browsers, with its favicon: `enter` switches to it, and you can close, mute or copy it from the list.

## What it does

- Tabs from Chrome, Safari and Firefox, and any Chromium browser with remote debugging on
- Tab titles show up in the main search, so typing a page's name finds it
- Filters for All, Playing sound and This window
- Close (`cmd+w`), mute (`cmd+m`), copy the address (`cmd+c`) or a markdown link (`cmd+shift+c`)
- Firefox tabs can be listed and focused, but not closed or muted

## Palettes

- Browser Tabs

pal/calc.caption: Comes with pal · Productivity
pal/calc.title: Calculator
pal/calc.markdown:
Answers what you type as you type it: arithmetic, units, currencies, percentages, dates, time zones and durations, with variables of your own.

## What it does

- Arithmetic, percentages and number bases: `2^10`, `15% of 240`, `255 to hex`
- Units as people type them: `5 km to miles`, `72 f to c`, `5 ft 3 in to cm`
- 30 currencies by code, symbol or name (`€12 to $`), rates updated daily
- Dates and time zones: `next friday`, `days until 25 dec`, `3pm istanbul to new york`
- Your own variables: `rent = 42000 try`, then `rent / 12`
- A second answer in the other form: the reverse conversion, a fraction, hex, the ISO date

## Palettes

- Calculator

![12 usd to try at the ECB's rate, the reverse as the second row; the pane shows the rate, its inverse and where it comes from](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/calc/screenshots/1-currency.png)

pal/github.caption: The pal registry · Developer
pal/github.title: GitHub
pal/github.markdown:
Your pull requests, issues, repositories and notifications, and a search over all of GitHub. Signs in through the gh CLI or a token.

## What it does

- Your pull requests, the ones waiting on your review and what merged this week, with checks and review state; mute one, or ignore it until it changes
- A pull request or issue in full: the body, latest comments and reviews, every check, who approved
- Your repositories, your organisation's and your stars; `cmd+e` opens the local clone in the editor
- Notifications by reason; `enter` opens the thread and marks it read, `space` in the popover reads it first
- Search all of GitHub as you type, your own work first; `is:pr`, `author:` and `label:` work as on GitHub
- Create an issue or a repository, check out a branch or merge, without leaving the keyboard

## Palettes

- Pull Requests
- Issues
- Repositories
- Notifications
- Search GitHub

pal/timer.caption: Comes with pal · Productivity
pal/timer.title: Timer
pal/timer.markdown:
Named countdown timers and pomodoros: the soonest one counts down on the bar and turns into an alarm when it ends. Built on the `timer` command line tool, so timers started in a terminal show up here too.

## What it does

- One row per timer, most urgent first, with the time left or when it ended
- Start one by typing `25m`, `90s` or `1h30m` and a name; optionally ring the phone when it ends
- `enter` pauses, resumes or dismisses; `cmd++` adds minutes (five when none are typed); `cmd+d` stops
- Pomodoro: 25 minutes of work, 5 of break, 15 after the fourth round; `cmd+s` skips a phase
- A bar item with the countdown filling blue to amber to red; its popover pauses, adds time or starts a timer
- The same timers as the `timer` CLI, so one started in a terminal is in this list

## Palettes

- Timers

![Every timer, the most urgent first: one that just landed, three running with when each lands, one paused, and the pomodoros done today](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/timer/screenshots/1-timers.png)
![A running timer's actions: pause it, stop it, or add the minutes in the field beside the search (five unless you type more)](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/timer/screenshots/2-actions.png)
![A pomodoro round is a timer too: its row says the round and the phase, and skips to the break or stops the cycle](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/timer/screenshots/3-pomodoro.png)
![New timer, typed after the search: a duration as you would say it, an optional name, and whether the phone rings when it lands](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/timer/screenshots/4-new.png)

pal/onepassword.caption: The pal registry · Integration
pal/onepassword.title: 1Password
pal/onepassword.markdown:
Your 1Password items from the keyboard, through the op command line tool. Enter copies the password; the username, the one-time code and the item in the app are one key away.

## What it does

- Every item you can see, favourites first, with the vault, the username and the website
- `enter` copies the password, `cmd+u` the username, `cmd+t` the current one-time code
- `cmd+o` opens the item in the 1Password app
- Search by website, username, category, vault or tag, so `github.com` finds the login
- Secrets are fetched only when you copy one and never kept in the list, the index or a log
- Signed out, or without the op tool, one row says how to sign in or where to get it

## Palettes

- 1Password

![Items with their vault, username and website, favourites first](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/onepassword/screenshots/1-items.png)
![The detail pane (cmd+I): the vault over the title, its category and tags, the username, website and when it changed](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/onepassword/screenshots/2-detail.png)
![Copy the password, the username or the one-time code, or open the app](https://pal.cagdas.io/extensions/onepassword/screenshots/3-actions.png)

pal/otp.caption: The pal registry · Integration
pal/otp.title: Verification Codes
pal/otp.markdown:
One-time codes from your recent text messages, newest first, with who sent them. Enter pastes the code into the app in front; a bar item shows a new code as it arrives.

## What it does

- Codes from the last 24 hours of Messages on macOS, newest first, the sender named from Contacts
- Spots codes in English and Turkish messages, skipping amounts, dates and phone numbers
- A code that just arrived is the first row and shows up at the root
- A bar item shows the newest code for a minute, with the sender and the codes before it
- Copied codes stay out of clipboard history, and the previous clipboard comes back after 30 seconds

## Palettes
